summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of kidney transplant, coronary artery disease, prior pulmonary embolism, and heart failure presented with sudden-onset pleuritic chest pain and dyspnea, concerning for pulmonary embolism. She was transferred on empiric heparin. Initial chest X-ray was clear, and troponins were negative. A V/Q scan showed very low likelihood of pulmonary embolism, followed by a contrast CT angiogram that confirmed no embolism or aortic abnormality. Her chest pain improved during hospitalization. Creatinine rose from 1.8 to 2.3 likely due to contrast exposure, consistent with acute kidney injury. Tacrolimus dose was reduced from 2 mg to 1.5 mg twice daily based on therapeutic drug levels. She was discharged home with instructions to follow up with cardiology for a stress test or echocardiogram and to monitor kidney function with outpatient labs.
problems: Atherosclerotic heart disease of native coronary artery without angina pectoris
